published_prior_art.cite: Molinari2008 gives general direct-misclassification partial identification; ZhangNieSoonLiu2013 reconstructs a fixed-margin binary table at a fixed odds ratio, neither gives the shared-channel finite candidate envelope.
CiocaneaTeodorescuGabrielSjolander2025 treats clean-outcome probability-of-benefit sensitivity with positive cells, not closure-to-strict attainment under an uncertain shared assay.
ZhangNieSoonLiu2013 supplies the fixed-clean-margin odds reconstruction; the uncertain-assay exact example is a diagnostic specialization.
KaidoMolinariStoye2019 provides asymptotic calibrated projection and GabrielSachsJensen2024 studies bootstrap inference, not exact four-binomial shared-assay projection through the finite envelope.
KaidoMolinariStoye2019 gives generic asymptotic projection inference; the stated finite-sample Youden-index modulus is specialized to the new envelope.
No checked cited source studies a matching universal lower bound for endpoint-evaluation complexity of the shared-channel benefit envelope.

source_verification_receipts.version: JRSS C journal version of record, Volume 62 Issue 5 (2013)
source_verification_receipts.locator: publisher front matter; corroborating author manuscript, Section 2.3 and Section 3.3, especially the fixed-margin odds-ratio reconstruction discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper exists at the cited venue/year and studies binary potential-outcome tables using an odds-ratio sensitivity analysis; it is an appropriate fixed-clean-margin comparator, not a shared-assay envelope result.
The article presents the direct-misclassification approach as a linear simultaneous system linking latent and observed discrete distributions under restricted misclassification probabilities.

The paper studies probability-of-benefit sensitivity analysis in binary randomized trials through departure from conditional independence of potential outcomes, with strict positive-cell discussion; it does not state an uncertain common-assay candidate-map theorem.
The article derives symbolic ordinal benefit bounds and reports regular-bootstrap undercoverage near boundaries together with conservative m-out-of-n behavior.
The paper proposes bootstrap calibrated projection for components and smooth functions in moment-(in)equality models with uniform asymptotic coverage, rather than exact binomial projection.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a concise analytic comparison proving where the ten-candidate evaluator strictly improves on a specified general-program formulation, including a reproducible nonvertex-contact instance and complexity accounting.
Strengthen the inference contribution by optimizing the Bonferroni allocation over validation and trial strata, with an explicit width-optimal allocation rule or a certified approximation guarantee.
Add a boundary corollary characterizing the exact behavior as the Youden floor tends to zero or as the odds band expands, separating genuine instability from removable algebraic contacts.

recommended_next_step: Advance the shared-assay envelope to Stage 0, retaining the finite-map theorem as the field-tier kernel and treating exact projection as its attached inference rung.
